card.title: Reports and summaries — facts first, words few

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Class 12 writing goes professional: reports (event/factual — headline, byline, lead with 5Ws, body in descending importance, no opinion), summaries and note-making (≤1/3 length, own words, key points only), articles (opinion + evidence for publication), reviews (book/film: premise → craft → verdict), paraphrasing (same meaning, new sentence structures). Essays, letters, emails, stories, speeches and dialogues carry over from Class 11 at higher polish.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: report: HEADLINE + byline + lead (who/what/when/where) + body (why/how, descending) + tail  ·  summary: read → underline → draft (own words, ~1/3) → check (no examples/opinions)  ·  review: premise + craft (plot/style/acting) + verdict + rating logic  ·  paraphrase: change structure + synonyms, keep facts

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Reports stay objective (witness voice, past tense, attributed quotes). Summaries keep the original's ORDER and proportion (one idea, one weight). Reviews may judge but must evidence (scene/technique cited). Paraphrases must survive back-translation (meaning intact) to count.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Newspaper vs school-magazine reports differ in headline punch but share the lead-body skeleton. Flowchart notes compress processes; tree notes compress hierarchies. Email upgrades letters with subject-line precision and CC discipline. Story openers (dialogue/mystery/action) beat weather clichés.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Summarise a 300-word passage in 100: read twice, underline one key sentence per paragraph, merge into own-word sentences keeping order, delete examples/repetition/opinion, count words, verify nothing essential dropped. The four-pass method hits length AND fidelity together.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Templates organise but cannot invent content — empty reports fail regardless of shape. Over-compression drops qualifications (summaries lie by omission). Review subjectivity needs declared criteria, else verdicts read as whims.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From the mark scheme backward: content (facts complete) + organisation (lead-first, coherent) + language (concise, accurate) → the report lead answers all five Ws in two lines because editors cut from the bottom; summaries keep proportion because graders check coverage per original paragraph.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Report: 5Ws in the lead, details descending. Summary: own words, one-third, no examples. Review: verdict needs two evidenced reasons. Paraphrase: flip active/passive + swap synonyms + reorder clauses.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: event report with headline + lead; summary/note-making to length; article with thesis + evidence; book/film review with verdict; paraphrase passage holding meaning.
